subject: HealthBridge: audit log exportability & compliance next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Alvarez <jenna.alvarez@healthbridge.com>, Liam Chen <liam.chen@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — audit logs, exportability, next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery on audit logging and compliance: 

- Requirements you called out: admin activity logs (console + API), request/response API logs, retention policy ~7 years with legal-hold capability, and an immutable/exportable archive for audits.
- You asked about SOC 2 status, GDPR/HIPAA applicability, and the process for the vendor security questionnaire.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Can you please share the vendor security questionnaire (I’ve added a placeholder attachment field below) so our security team can start filling it out?
2) Marissa (cc) to propose a technical deep-dive next week to go over fields, sample exports, and immutability options.
3) I’ll pull together an initial mapping of which Redwood logs contain the fields you called out and sample retention/export workflows.

Attachments: redwood-security-highlights.pdf (high level SOC/HIPAA summary)

Anything I missed from your side? If that timeline looks good I’ll have Marissa reach out with available slots for the deep-dive.

—
Markus Klein
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Jenna Alvarez <jenna.alvarez@healthbridge.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam Chen <liam.chen@healthbridge.com>, security@healthbridge.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — audit logs, exportability, next steps

Thanks Markus — good summary. Attaching our standard vendor security questionnaire (HealthBridge-Vendor-Q.docx). A few clarifications up-front: 

- SOC 2: we need to review your most recent SOC 2 Type II report and any system description notes relevant to logging. Is that available?
- Export targets: we prefer S3-compatible exports into a customer-controlled bucket (or SFTP as a fallback). Exports must support WORM/immutability or be accompanied by a signed hash chain for evidentiary purposes.
- Retention & legal hold: default retention is 7 years, with the ability to freeze export/deletion under legal hold.

Can Marissa confirm whether Redwood can:
- Produce per-tenant admin activity logs and API request logs with timestamps, actor identifiers, IPs, and request IDs;
- Export a daily compacted archive (newline-delimited JSON or Parquet) to an S3 bucket; and
- Provide immutability guarantees (either via write-once object store or signed digest chain)?

We’d like a proposed timeline for the questionnaire turnaround and a slot for a technical deep-dive next week (our preferred times are Tue/Wed mornings PST).

Thanks —
Jenna Alvarez
Sr. Security Program Manager, HealthBridge
jenna.alvarez@healthbridge.com

Attachment: healthbridge-vendor-questionnaire.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Alvarez <jenna.alvarez@healthbridge.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — audit logs, exportability, next steps

Hi Jenna — copying from our internal notes and providing concrete answers to your bullet points. Apologies for the longer note, I wanted to be explicit so procurement/security have something to review before the deep-dive.

Short answers up-front:
- SOC 2: Redwood holds a SOC 2 Type II report (issue date: 2024-11). We can provide an access-controlled read-only link to the report and a scoped system description. See related link in the metadata above.
- Log types: we produce per-tenant admin activity logs (console logins, role changes, user provisioning), API request logs (timestamp, request_id, caller_id, endpoint, response_code, request_size, response_size), model-inference telemetry (token counts, latency), and job lifecycle events.
- Fields available: timestamp, actor email/ID, actor IP, request_id, session_id, action, resource, parameters (redacted by policy), outcome/status. If you have a canonical field list please share and we’ll map directly.
- Export formats & delivery: we support daily exports as newline-delimited JSON or Parquet. Exports can be pushed to a customer-owned S3 bucket (preferred) via an assumed-role ACL or delivered to an SFTP endpoint.
- Immutability/evidence: for S3 exports we support a WORM lifecycle using the bucket’s Object Lock in governance mode, plus we can provide a signed Merkle-like digest chain for exported archive batches if you need cryptographic verification. Internally applied write-once logs are retained as append-only segments for the configured retention period.
- Retention & legal hold: retention policies are configurable per-account; legal hold can be initiated by our compliance team and will pause deletion for the requested period.

Attachments: audit-log-specs.pdf — contains sample schemas and a short runbook for S3 export configuration.

Proposed next steps: 
1) I’ll start filling out the vendor questionnaire you attached; please expect a first pass in 3 business days.
2) Let’s schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive (we can do Tue 10 May 10:00–11:00 PST or Wed 11 May 09:00–10:00 PST). Markus / Ben will attend for commercial questions.
3) If you can confirm the exact fields and retention triggers (e.g., legal hold flow), we’ll include those in the runbook and SOW language.

If you need any attestations for HIPAA specifically we can route that through our compliance counsel — call that out in the questionnaire and we’ll escalate.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0124

Thanks, looking forward to the deep-dive.

Jenna Alvarez
